verdict.rationale: Logseq ships a documented local HTTP API server, enabled in settings, with bearer-token auth and CORS. Its single POST /api endpoint dispatches any plugin-API method (logseq.Editor, logseq.DB, etc.), so an external agent can read and write the graph, as the worked curl examples show. Missing for 10: an OpenAPI or machine-readable spec (probes 404), llms.txt, a versioning policy, first-party rather than community-driven method docs, and hands-on independent corroboration; access is also local-only and requires the desktop app running.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: we developed the local HTTP server to support external access to the database through authorization.
Enable HTTP APIs server in `Features > HTTP APIs server`
POST `/api` - `method` can be any of the ones listed in https://plugins-doc.logseq.com/. `args` is an array of arguments to pass to method.
-d '{"method": "logseq.Editor.insertBlock", "args": ["Test page", "This is a new block", {"isPageBlock": true}]}'
logseq.App logseq.Editor logseq.DB logseq.Git logseq.UI logseq.Assets logseq.FileStorage
